Certification Categories in India

The Central Board of Film Certification classifies films according to their suitability for different audiences. The classifications are intended to distinguish unrestricted viewing, parental guidance, adult-only viewing and exhibition restricted to specialised audiences.

The Cinematograph (Amendment) Act, 2023 and the Cinematograph (Certification) Rules, 2024 introduced and implemented important changes to the certification framework.

The age-based UA classifications became operational from 24 October 2024, as announced by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting on 15 November 2024. The CBFC's revised certification guidelines notified in September 2026 retain the age-based classification framework.

Applicable Categories as of 26 November 2026

CertificateMeaning
UUnrestricted public exhibition; suitable for general audiences.
UA 7+Parental guidance advised for children below 7 years.
UA 13+Parental guidance advised for children below 13 years.
UA 16+Parental guidance advised for children below 16 years.
APublic exhibition restricted to adults aged 18 years or above.
SPublic exhibition restricted to a specified profession or class of persons.

Parental Guidance Is Different from a Legal Age Restriction

The UA markers provide information to parents or lawful guardians about the suitability of a film for children.

For example, a UA 13+ certificate advises parents to consider whether a child below 13 years should watch the film. It does not create an absolute prohibition on viewing by every child below that age.

An A certificate operates differently. It restricts public exhibition to adults, meaning persons who have completed 18 years of age.

An S certificate restricts exhibition to a specified profession or class of persons according to the nature of the film. It is not a higher age category.

Earlier and revised UA categories

Older study material may describe a single UA classification associated with parental guidance for children below 12 years. For questions concerning the applicable revised framework, remember the 3 UA age markers: 7+, 13+ and 16+.

Validity of Film Certificates

Before the 2023 amendment, Section 5A of the Cinematograph Act prescribed a validity period of 10 years for a film certificate.

The Cinematograph (Amendment) Act, 2023 removed this 10-year limit. Certificates are now valid throughout India without that fixed expiry period, subject to other provisions of the Act, including lawful suspension or revocation.

Therefore, a certificate having continuing validity does not mean that it can never be suspended or revoked.

Consolidated Revision of Indian and Gujarati Cinema

The principal facts of Indian and Gujarati cinema can be organised into historical milestones, performing arts traditions, recognition, social influence and legal regulation.

For objective examinations, it is particularly important to distinguish film directors from literary authors, silent films from talkies, regional cinema from parallel cinema, lifetime honours from film-specific awards, and parental guidance from mandatory viewing restrictions.

Prelims focus

  • Current UA markers: UA 7+, UA 13+ and UA 16+.
  • UA markers provide parental guidance rather than absolute age restrictions.
  • A certificate: adults aged 18 years or above.
  • S certificate: specified profession or class of persons.
  • The 2023 amendment removed the fixed 10-year validity limit.
  • Certification remains subject to the Cinematograph Act and constitutional safeguards.

[References: India Code, Cinematograph Act, 1952, Sections 4, 5A, 5B and 5E; Cinematograph (Amendment) Act, 2023; Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Cinematograph (Certification) Rules, 2024; Press Information Bureau, CBFC Introduces New Film Certification Categories for Public Exhibition, 15 November 2024, Release ID 2073592; CBFC official FAQ and Revised Guidelines for Certification, September 2026. Legal and certification status consulted as of 26 November 2026.]
